_comment: Shipped defaults for rules-by-path. Two more layers may override these,
its numbers are clamped). `rules-by-path config --root <root>` prints the
effective result and says which layer each block came from.
rule_types is replaced whole by the nearest layer that declares it; the
other keys are merged key by key.
Only prohibition-shaped constraints are known to decay under long context
(arXiv:2604.20911), so only BUSN defaults to active reinforcement; the
other types default to never and pay reinforcement's cost only when a
rule opts back in. reinject_budget caps how many times ANY rule may be
re-injected in one session, regardless of type or distance covered.
language is what rule BODIES are written in — the manage skill reads it
and drafts in that language — and also what the text the hook injects
around them comes out in, whenever the plugin ships a translation of it
(en, pt-BR). Any other language is still a fine value: the rules are
written in it and only that surrounding text falls back to English.
Rule file names, type prefixes and frontmatter keys never translate.
